checks.after: Shi Hu again sent Shi Cheng against Fancheng without success but seized Guangcheng.
checks.reason: Chinese 又使 is omitted in the original EN; restoring again matches 季龍又使石成入攻凡城 and is not a style-only change.

checks.after: Moreover, when Murong Huang learned that Yu Liang had died and Yu Bing and Yu Yi had succeeded as generals and ministers, he submitted a memorial: Your servant has closely observed the muddled and clear rulers of former ages; if they could treat the worthy with intimacy and elevate them together, then merit reached peaceful ascendancy;
checks.reason: Original EN drops 又, softens 繼為將相 to held power, and flattens 昏明/臣究觀/親賢並建; the proposed after restores those source propositions.

checks.after: If one could change course, overturn and collapse can be avoided.
checks.reason: 苟能易軌 is conditional if one can change course, and 覆墜 is overturn and collapse; in time is not in the Chinese.

checks.after: Your Majesty is heaven-born to the age, destined to exalt Jin's Way, yet has encountered many hardships of state; deep grief presses on every side, and recalling past affairs still burns with anguish to this day.
checks.reason: 命世天挺 and 當隆晉道 are two linked claims, and 殷憂/至今楚灼 are under-rendered in the original EN; the after restores them without inventing content.

checks.after: Tracing where it came from, it was truly because the late Minister of Works Yu Liang occupied the honor of chief maternal uncle and the weight of power and achievement, governed and judged subordinates, and lightly insulted frontier generals, so that Su Jun and Zu Yue could not contain their rage and thus brought disaster on the state.
checks.reason: Original EN invents harshly for 輕侮 and drops 跡其所由/勢業之重; lightly insulted and the tracing clause match the Chinese.

checks.after: Past events, if not forgotten, are a model for later affairs; yet Yu Bing, Director of the Secretariat and General of the Left, and his fellows grasp the pivot within and hold senior military commands outside; the brothers stand side by side, with no other minister to match them.
checks.reason: 前事不忘 is past events if not forgotten, not merely remembering; the after restores 不忘 and keeps the pivot/command structure.

checks.after: Your Majesty deeply honors the ties of Weiyang; Bing and his fellows ought themselves to stretch their necks in expectation.
checks.reason: 渭陽 is the Weiyang maternal-uncle allusion, not generic family ties; 自宜引領 is themselves stretch necks, which the after preserves.

checks.after: Your servant often says: if a ruler of the age wishes to honor the maternal clan, why not enfeoff them with vassal states, enrich their stipends and gifts, and limit their power and advantage, so that above there is no partial favor and below no private talk.
checks.reason: 何不 is a why-not question, not an imperative; 祿賜/勢利/私論 are gifts, advantage, and private talk, which the original EN understates or shifts.

checks.after: Your servant and Bing and the others differ in rank and status and are far apart in our situations; moreover, they are close kin of the imperial house. By rights I ought to defer and accommodate myself to the circumstances.
checks.reason: 臣與冰等 requires Bing and the others, and 國之戚昵 refers to them as close imperial kin; the after corrects the dropped 等 and speaker framing.

checks.after: I wear disheveled hair in a foreign land, hold the rank of supreme general, worry day and night and know not how to repay, and can only destroy enemies abroad, exhaust loyal remonstrance within, and exert strength and offer sincerity to answer the state's grace.
checks.reason: Original EN truncates 陳力輸誠，以答國恩 and softens 位為上將/罔知所報/內盡忠規; the after restores those closing source clauses.

checks.after: That year he invaded Goguryeo; King Gao Zhao begged a covenant and he withdrew.
checks.reason: 乞盟 is begged a covenant, a specific pact request; sued for peace understates that source wording.

checks.after: Huang was about to plan against the Shi clan; he calmly told the generals: “Shi Hu thinks the cities of Anle and the rest are strictly and heavily guarded, and surely sets no defenses north and south of the city; now if we take a deceitful route and strike where he does not expect, the whole northern territory of Ji can be broken.”
checks.reason: 城之南北 is north and south of the city, 冀之北土 is northern Ji, and 從容/詭路 are omitted; wall and whole Ji plain are source errors.

checks.after: Emperor Cheng then sent concurrent Grand Herald Guo Xi bearing credentials to appoint Huang Palace Attendant, Grand Commander of all military affairs north of the Yellow River, Grand General, and King of Yan, leaving the rest of his offices as before.
checks.reason: 兼大鴻臚 and 持節 are definite omissions, and 大都督河北諸軍事 is commander of military affairs north of the Yellow River, not a vague north of the river.

checks.after: He took forty thousand picked soldiers through the southern defile against Yuwen and Goguryeo, with Murong Han and his son Murong Chui as vanguard, and sent chief clerk Wang Yu and others leading fifteen thousand to advance from Beizhi.
checks.reason: 勁卒 is picked soldiers, 翰及子垂 names Han and his son Chui, and 長史王寓等 is chief clerk Wang Yu and others; veterans and the dropped titles are source defects.

checks.after: King Gao Zhao assumed Huang’s army was coming by the northern route, so he sent his younger brother Wu leading fifty thousand picked troops to block Beizhi, and personally led weaker troops to guard the southern defile.
checks.reason: 精銳 and 躬率 are definite omissions; the after restores picked troops and that Zhao personally led the weaker southern guard.

checks.after: Yuwen Gui sent his state chancellor Moqian Hun against Huang; Huang’s generals begged to fight but he refused.
checks.reason: 國相 is state chancellor and 伐皝 is against Huang; both are omitted in the original EN and restored here.

checks.after: Murong Huang personally toured his prefectures and counties, urged farming and sericulture, and raised palaces at Longcheng.
checks.reason: 躬巡郡縣 is personally toured prefectures and counties; domains and the dropped 躬 understate the Chinese.

checks.after: Yuwen Gui sent his cavalry general Sheyiyu to hold Murong Han with the whole host; Huang sent word at a gallop: “Sheyiyu is fierce and bold; you ought to avoid him a little, wait until the bandits grow arrogant, then take them.”
checks.reason: 宜小避之 means slightly avoid him, not spar lightly; 騎將/盡眾/馳遣/雄悍 are also under-rendered or omitted in the original EN.

checks.after: He then advanced to battle, beheaded Sheyiyu, and wholly captured their host; Gui fled far to the northern desert.
checks.reason: 歸遠遁漠北 makes Gui the one who fled far to the northern desert; drove Yuwen Gui deep into the steppe reverses the subject.

checks.after: He opened over a thousand li of territory, moved more than fifty thousand of their tribal settlements to Changli, and changed Sheyiyu city to Weide city.
checks.reason: 開地千餘里 is opened over a thousand li of territory, and 五萬餘落 counts settlements, not dependents; pasture and dependents are source errors.

additionalCorrections.before: Huang said, “Moqian Hun’s arrogance has peaked—now we can strike.”
additionalCorrections.after: Huang said, “Moqian Hun’s extravagance and jealousy are already extreme; now then we can fight.”
additionalCorrections.sourceQuote: 皝曰：「渾奢忌已甚，今則可一戰矣。」
additionalCorrections.sourceReason: 奢忌 means extravagance and jealousy or suspicion, not arrogance; 今則可一戰矣 is now then one can fight, so the EN must not substitute a different charge.

additionalCorrections.before: Sheyiyu is overrated and brittle—we must not let him sap our morale.”
additionalCorrections.after: Sheyiyu vainly has an empty name; in truth he is easy to deal with; we ought not to loose the enemy and blunt our army’s spirit.”
additionalCorrections.sourceQuote: 奕于徒有虛名，其實易與耳，不宜縱敵挫吾兵氣。」
additionalCorrections.sourceReason: 易與 means easy to deal with, not brittle, and 不宜縱敵挫吾兵氣 is ought not to loose the enemy and blunt our army’s spirit.
